mainEntity.name: What is a crypto PR agency in Singapore and who is it for?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Singapore crypto PR operator helps blockchain, DeFi, RWA, DePIN and AI-layer founders get coverage in regional and global outlets, build credibility with the MAS-adjacent investor community, and leverage Token2049 to place stories at scale. The right fit for most founders is a fractional senior operator rather than a full agency, because the window for Token2049 and SEA fundraising cycles is short and you need someone who knows the editors personally. Shilika Jain runs APAC crypto PR directly for $5K–$12K/month, with placements in CoinDesk, e27, The Block and Forbes.

mainEntity.name: How much does crypto PR cost in Singapore?

acceptedAnswer.text: Singapore-based full-service agencies typically charge $15K–$45K/month, covering a team of account executives, PR managers and regional translators. A fractional senior operator delivers the same senior scope for $5K–$12K/month by removing the team markup. A Token2049-focused launch sprint runs $15K–$40K over four to eight weeks, covering pre-event embargo strategy, on-the-ground outreach and post-event follow-through. KOL activation is priced separately: nano influencers $200–$1.5K per post, micro $500–$5K, mid-tier $10K–$30K.

mainEntity.name: Which outlets can you place my project in for Singapore and SEA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regional English-language: e27, Tech in Asia, CoinDesk APAC, The Block, Blockworks, Forkast. mainEntity.name: What is the process and timeline for Token2049 PR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Preparation starts six weeks before Token2049: narrative positioning, journalist briefings and embargo letter distribution. Four weeks before the event, embargoed briefings go to key outlets. One week before, KOL seeding and side-event coordination run in parallel. On the day, staged release timing keeps the story in the feed for 48 hours. Post-event, follow-up features and podcast placements compound the initial coverage.
